knowledge.statement: append on a non-leader creates one ProposalForward message addressed to the current leader and moves the entries into it; the core keeps no copy for retry. resend_messages_follower resends only the cached Promise (Prepare phase) or PrepareReq (Recover), and resend_messages_leader resends Prepare, AcceptStopSign and the StopSign's Decide. A ProposalForward lost in transport, or received by a leader that fails before accepting it, is therefore not re-proposed by the core; the caller's transport and any application-level retry carry that duty. The runtime layer's TaggedProposal path does retry undispatched proposals on ticks, which is a separate, stronger contract.

knowledge.statement: When the outgoing channel does not accept a message, messages accumulate in outgoing_buf; once its length exceeds the channel capacity (or max_outgoing_buffered), drain_outgoing_buf drops the oldest entries before retrying. The same buffer holds core protocol traffic pulled by flush_outgoing, including PaxosMsg::ProposalForward produced when a plain append is issued on a follower, and runtime control messages enqueued by try_dispatch_undispatched (TaggedProposal) and by Assigned replies. Core resends Promise/PrepareReq/Prepare/AcceptStopSign/StopSign-Decide but not ProposalForward, and the runtime does not resend TaggedProposal, so dropping those messages loses the corresponding client proposal (a tagged proposal then resolves only by timeout; a plain forwarded append is not retried at all). The configuration docs justify drop-oldest as safe because OmniPaxos tolerates lost messages, which covers protocol messages but not these client-origin ones.
knowledge.conditions: Runtime actor with outgoing channel backpressure sustained long enough for outgoing_buf to exceed its cap while client-origin messages are queued; the caller is expected to drain outgoing_messages continuously, so sustained non-draining is a caller-duty violation and bounds the applicability.

interpretations.rationale: The pending completion path can report a false success, under a schedule the actor does not exclude. A pending append_notify keeps only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot). drain_notifiers evaluates, in order, Ok when assigned_idx <= decided, then Superseded when the assignment ballot is below the current promise ballot, then Timeout; the Ok arm reads no log entry and never checks that the value at assigned_idx is the caller's entry. The origin can hold an assignment made when it was leader or when a leader accepted its proposal, lose leadership to a higher ballot, and then have its own decided index advance past assigned_idx with a different value at that index: the runtime's own Superseded regression test constructs exactly that replacement (the old leader accepts locally with its outgoing cut, a new leader appends a fresh entry that decides at the same index, and the origin learns of the new ballot). Whether the pending resolves Ok or Superseded then depends only on whether a drain runs after the promise advanced but before decided reached assigned_idx. drain_notifiers runs only in the actor's tick branch; handling an incoming message never drains. Nothing orders a tick between the ballot change and the decided advance, so when the origin processes the higher-ballot Prepare and then the message that carries decided >= assigned_idx within one tick interval, the Ok arm wins and the caller is told its entry is decided at an index that holds a different entry. With a legal user-set tick_period that exceeds the leadership-turnover interval, that ordering is deterministic; with a short period it is a race. The gap on the reachable schedule is therefore answered on source grounds: no mechanism prevents it, and a legal configuration makes it the expected ordering.

3f84facd1a81451882518e32ee8be535-gap-0.explanation: Reachable. drain_notifiers is invoked only from the tick branch (actor.rs tick handling), while handle_incoming_tracked processes messages without draining; the actor polls the tick first each iteration but the tick fires at most once per configured period. investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. history.question: Can a follower that holds an accepted StopSign be left behind, with its decided index stuck at the StopSign's position, when the current leader's decided index has advanced beyond its own log and the leader's Decides are the follower's next expected sequence messages?
history.hypothesis: An AcceptSync whose prefix already covers the StopSign but which also carries it makes sync_log add one to the accepted index without placing an entry, so the accepted index lands one past the readable log, the marker is relocated to the inflated position and the StopSign loses its decided status because decided no longer equals accepted. knowledge.statement: Pending append_notify calls in the runtime actor are resolved in this order: Ok(idx) when the recorded assignment index is <= the actor's current decided index; Superseded when the assignment ballot is lower than the current promise ballot; Timeout when the deadline passed; otherwise the pending stays queued. The Ok arm is evaluated first and does not inspect the log or compare the entry stored at idx.
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor, append_notify tracking enabled; pending entry has an assigned (idx, ballot) from local accept or a remote Assigned reply; drain_notifiers runs on each actor tick and after command handling.

knowledge.statement: The runtime's test suite treats a successful append_notify as a claim that the caller's entry is decided at the returned index: the batching regression test reads the decided log back and asserts the value at the returned index equals the submitted entry, so a returned index holding a different value is a contract violation under the project's own expectation.
knowledge.conditions: The test environment's exercised conditions: 3-node runtime cluster with real transport, batching enabled, and a submitted append_notify entry; this is an individual test expectation plus the handle-level description, not a proof of a defect by itself.

knowledge.statement: The Superseded regression test demonstrates that an entry accepted only on the old leader can be genuinely lost and replaced at the same log index by a different value under the new leader, and that Superseded is the intended observable in that case; it also shows the origin node learns of the new higher-ballot leader.
knowledge.conditions: 3-node runtime cluster, the elected leader's outgoing traffic is cut while its incoming traffic stays open; a new leader is elected by the other two nodes and a fresh entry is appended and decided at the old index.

knowledge.statement: With decided=6 and compacted=4 on the executed two-node log, read_decided_suffix(1) returned exactly [Trimmed(4), Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 3) although decided-from is 5, while read_decided_suffix(4) returned [Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 2). The trimmed prefix is represented by a single Trimmed element, so the returned vector length is not the number of requested log indices when the start is below the compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Two OmniPaxos instances (pids 1,2) built from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 becomes leader via try_become_leader, appends Value(1..=6) with full message delivery after each append, then trims to 4 and the trim is forwarded to node 2; both nodes report decided 6.

knowledge.statement: Applied to those real read_decided_suffix outputs, one cursor step per returned element (the actor's push_to_sub rule) leaves next_idx at 4 after the catch-up from 1, and the next push_to_all_subs read from 4 yields entries 5 and 6 again, so the delivered value sequence is 5,6,5,6 with duplicates of 5 and 6 while decided remains 6 and no new entry was decided.
knowledge.conditions: Same executed setup as @suffix_collapse_observed; the cursor replay reproduces omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs push_to_sub (next_idx += 1 per element) and one subsequent push_to_all_subs read from the resulting cursor (start = 0 for a single subscriber). The replay is a reconstruction of the runtime source logic over executed core outputs, not an execution of the runtime crate.

knowledge.statement: On the executed five-node run, node 5 had decided through index 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)); after the new leader's AcceptSync it reported decided 4 and read index 4 as Undecided(Value(5)); after the new leader re-decided index 5 it reported decided 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)) again. The same log index was therefore observed Decided, Undecided and Decided with unchanged value.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5), ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,3,4,5]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots. Entry 5 is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided by leader 1, but the Decide reaches only node 5; nodes 2 and 3 stay decided 4 with accepted 5. Node 1 is then cut, node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 only (decided 4), and node 5's Prepare is delivered only after node 2 is in Accept, so its Promise is handled by handle_promise_accept and answered with an AcceptSync carrying decided 4.

knowledge.statement: A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum (handle_majority_promises -> get_max_decided_idx). A follower whose Promise arrives after that quorum is answered by handle_promise_accept with send_accsync stamped with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which assigns it to the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that had already learned a later decision therefore loses decided progress until the new leader re-accepts and re-decides the entry.
knowledge.conditions: Majority quorum with five nodes; at least one member of the new leader's prepare quorum accepted the entry without deciding it; the more-informed follower is delayed past the quorum; no snapshots involved in the sync.

knowledge.statement: With a single lost Prepare and the public reconnected(2) call, node 5's decided index fell from 5 to 4 and read(4) changed from Decided(Value(5)) to Undecided(Value(5)) after the new leader's Accept-phase AcceptSync; after the new leader re-decided index 5, node 5 returned to decided 5 and Decided(Value(5)). The observed message sequence was PrepareReq from node 5, Prepare to node 5, Promise from node 5, AcceptSync to node 5 and an Accepted reply, with lost_prepare_count 1.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5), MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots. Entry 5 is decided by leader 1 with nodes 1,2,3,5 accepting but the Decide reaching only node 5; node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 (decided 4); the Prepare addressed to node 5 is dropped; the probe calls node5.reconnected(2) as the documented re-establish-connection entry point.

knowledge.statement: Entries appended while this node is leader in Phase::Prepare are pushed to buffered_proposals. When the node later receives an AcceptSync (after promising a leader, whether in the prepare phase or in the accept phase), handle_acceptsync calls forward_buffered_proposals before switching to Phase::Accept; that call takes the whole buffer and forwards it to the current leader if there is no accepted StopSign. The buffered entries are therefore re-proposed rather than stranded when leadership moves away before the prepare quorum completes.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos with no accepted StopSign; the node promises a subsequent leader and receives its AcceptSync; the forwarded ProposalForward is delivered to that leader (normal message delivery).

knowledge.statement: SequencePaxos::snapshot passes its index to InternalStorage::try_snapshot, which accepts any index less than the local decided index (equal maps to the decided index without the StopSign) and rejects only indices greater than decided with UndecidedIndex. It performs trim, compacted-index and snapshot writes atomically and never consults the minimum accepted index. The snapshot API is therefore not affected by the sparse-pid placeholders that block trim, so a snapshot-capable Entry type can still compact a configuration such as {1,2,5}.
knowledge.conditions: A snapshot-capable Entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) and a snapshot index not greater than the node's decided index; the node may be a follower when local_only is true.

knowledge.statement: create_log_sync sends the StopSign in a separate log_sync field and starts the suffix at the follower's valid entries index, then sync_log sets accepted_idx to sync_idx + suffix length and adds one more when log_sync carries a StopSign. When sync_idx already covers the StopSign (the follower's accepted prefix includes it), accepted_idx becomes one greater than the follower's last log position. Since nothing may be appended after an accepted StopSign, decided can reach at most that last position and stopsign_is_decided (decided == accepted) can never become true for that follower. When sync_idx precedes the StopSign, the same +1 is correct and the follower ends consistent.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos follower applying an AcceptSync whose log_sync carries a StopSign; the follower either already accepted that StopSign (sync_idx includes it; defect) or had not (sync_idx precedes it; correct). No snapshots involved.

knowledge.statement: append on a non-leader creates one ProposalForward message addressed to the current leader and moves the entries into it; the core keeps no copy for retry. resend_messages_follower resends only the cached Promise (Prepare phase) or PrepareReq (Recover), and resend_messages_leader resends Prepare, AcceptStopSign and the StopSign's Decide. A ProposalForward lost in transport, or received by a leader that fails before accepting it, is therefore not re-proposed by the core; the caller's transport and any application-level retry carry that duty. The runtime layer's TaggedProposal path does retry undispatched proposals on ticks, which is a separate, stronger contract.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos with entries appended on a node that is not the leader and no accepted StopSign; the scheduled tick-driven resend paths only; transport loss or leader failure before acceptance.

knowledge.statement: When the outgoing channel does not accept a message, messages accumulate in outgoing_buf; once its length exceeds the channel capacity (or max_outgoing_buffered), drain_outgoing_buf drops the oldest entries before retrying. The same buffer holds core protocol traffic pulled by flush_outgoing, including PaxosMsg::ProposalForward produced when a plain append is issued on a follower, and runtime control messages enqueued by try_dispatch_undispatched (TaggedProposal) and by Assigned replies. Core resends Promise/PrepareReq/Prepare/AcceptStopSign/StopSign-Decide but not ProposalForward, and the runtime does not resend TaggedProposal, so dropping those messages loses the corresponding client proposal (a tagged proposal then resolves only by timeout; a plain forwarded append is not retried at all). The configuration docs justify drop-oldest as safe because OmniPaxos tolerates lost messages, which covers protocol messages but not these client-origin ones.
knowledge.conditions: Runtime actor with outgoing channel backpressure sustained long enough for outgoing_buf to exceed its cap while client-origin messages are queued; the caller is expected to drain outgoing_messages continuously, so sustained non-draining is a caller-duty violation and bounds the applicability.

knowledge.statement: handle_accepted advances a leader's decided index to a follower-reported accepted index when that index exceeds the current decided index and is_chosen counts an accept quorum at or beyond it. is_chosen counts entries in accepted_indexes, which mixes the leader's own accepted index with follower indices reported in Accepted messages, and never inspects the log, so a leader can decide an index it has not locally accepted, including a StopSign accepted only by followers outside its prepare quorum. Because create_log_sync attaches only the leader's local StopSign, an AcceptSync issued by such a leader carries no StopSign, and resend_messages_leader's StopSign branch is guarded by get_stopsign(), so that leader sends neither AcceptStopSign nor the StopSign's Decide for the missing position.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos leader in Phase::Accept; a quorum of accepted_indexes reaches the reported index through the leader's own accepted index plus Accepted messages carrying the leader's ballot; the leader's prepare quorum did not merge a log_sync containing the StopSign, so its local log ends one position before the StopSign; no snapshots involved.

knowledge.statement: handle_majority_promises applies exactly one promise log_sync, the one kept as max_promise_sync while promises are collected in the Prepare phase. handle_promise_accept, the path for a Promise that arrives once the leader is already in the Accept phase, only records the promise metadata and sends that follower an AcceptSync; it never merges the Promise's log_sync into the leader's storage. A follower that accepted a StopSign and then promises after the prepare quorum therefore does not give the leader that StopSign, even though it is part of an accept quorum at the StopSign's index and reports that index in later Accepted replies, which is_chosen counts toward the leader's decision.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos leader that reached a prepare quorum without any log_sync containing the StopSign; the StopSign-holding follower's Promise arrives after the leader switched to Phase::Accept; no snapshots involved.

knowledge.statement: set_promise keeps only the log_sync of the greatest PromiseMetaData seen while promises are collected, and PromiseMetaData compares by n_accepted first and accepted_idx second. handle_majority_promises then applies that single log_sync. A follower whose Promise carries a later accept round but a shorter log is therefore greater than a follower whose Promise carries an earlier round and a longer log including an accepted StopSign, and the longer log's StopSign is never merged into the leader. The leader can hold a prepare quorum that intersects the StopSign holders and still reach Phase::Accept without the StopSign, which also means resend_messages_leader's StopSign branch, guarded by get_stopsign(), stays inactive for that position.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos leader collecting promises in Phase::Prepare; at least two promises differ in n_accepted or accepted_idx so only one wins the max comparison; the losing promise's log_sync is the only one containing the StopSign; no snapshots involved.

interpretations.rationale: The pending completion path can report a false success, under a schedule the actor does not exclude. A pending append_notify keeps only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot). drain_notifiers evaluates, in order, Ok when assigned_idx <= decided, then Superseded when the assignment ballot is below the current promise ballot, then Timeout; the Ok arm reads no log entry and never checks that the value at assigned_idx is the caller's entry. The origin can hold an assignment made when it was leader or when a leader accepted its proposal, lose leadership to a higher ballot, and then have its own decided index advance past assigned_idx with a different value at that index: the runtime's own Superseded regression test constructs exactly that replacement (the old leader accepts locally with its outgoing cut, a new leader appends a fresh entry that decides at the same index, and the origin learns of the new ballot). Whether the pending resolves Ok or Superseded then depends only on whether a drain runs after the promise advanced but before decided reached assigned_idx. drain_notifiers runs only in the actor's tick branch; handling an incoming message never drains. Nothing orders a tick between the ballot change and the decided advance, so when the origin processes the higher-ballot Prepare and then the message that carries decided >= assigned_idx within one tick interval, the Ok arm wins and the caller is told its entry is decided at an index that holds a different entry. With a legal user-set tick_period that exceeds the leadership-turnover interval, that ordering is deterministic; with a short period it is a race. The gap on the reachable schedule is therefore answered on source grounds: no mechanism prevents it, and a legal configuration makes it the expected ordering.

3f84facd1a81451882518e32ee8be535-gap-0.explanation: Reachable. drain_notifiers is invoked only from the tick branch (actor.rs tick handling), while handle_incoming_tracked processes messages without draining; the actor polls the tick first each iteration but the tick fires at most once per configured period. The ballot change (Prepare/AcceptSync from the new leader) and the decided advance (AcceptDecide/Decide from that leader) are separate messages that can both be processed inside one period. If the period exceeds the turnover interval, the pending sees decided >= assigned_idx and a stale assignment ballot at the same drain, and the Ok arm precedes the Superseded arm. Since tick_period is user-set and only advised to match the ServerConfig tick budget, this ordering is legal and deterministic in that configuration.

interpretations.rationale: Source establishes the mechanism but not yet the witness. handle_majority_promises sets the new leader's decided index to the maximum decided among the promises it has received (the prepare quorum); send_accsync then stamps every later promiser's AcceptSync with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which sets the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that promised during the prepare phase is part of that maximum; a follower whose Prepare is delayed until the leader is already in Accept is not, and set_promise for that later promise is called with check_max_prom false and does not update the maximum. If that follower had already learned a decision the quorum members had not, the AcceptSync lowers its decided index and read() reports a previously Decided entry as Undecided, contradicting the documented guarantee that a decided entry is not reverted and is safe to apply. The new leader then re-accepts and re-decides the entry after its accept quorum acknowledges, so the entry returns to Decided, exposing an at-least-once application hazard. The decisive uncertainty is whether the state can be built with real instances and legal message delays, which the registered five-node probe measures.

If every member of the new leader's prepare quorum has also received the earlier Decide, the leader's decided index already covers the entry and the sync is not lowering anything.
The value of the entry is preserved by the sync, so this is a visibility and application-status defect rather than a divergence of decided values.

materials.text:
- `Decided(T)`: The entry is decided and guaranteed to not be reverted. It is thus safe to apply a decided entry to the application state. For instance, in our case, it is safe to update our key-value store when we read a `Decided(KeyValue)` entry.
- `Undecided(T)`: The entry is NOT decided and might be removed from the log at a later time. However, it could be useful in applications that allow speculative execution for example.
